Everything should be running in a background task which would have a panic handler. But maybe OOM or something? Maybe some issue between siwe and the sequencer? no once you've done siwe the sequencer manages your session id I mean that theres an issue passing the session id from siwe to the sequencer Also the sessionid is always the same Oh if the sessionid is always the same then the sequencer isn't crashing here it's deduplicated by the sequencer with an in-memory mapping based on your eth address: ```rs if let Some(session_id) = state.unique_id_session.get(&user_data.unique_id()) { session_id.clone() } else { let id = SessionId::new(); state .unique_id_session .insert(user_data.unique_id(), id.clone()); id } ``` Which step do you get invalid session on? try contribute the first call to try contribute, right? all ah I see It always work after 5 minutes Is there some timeout in the code? Ah I bet that's it, it doesn't expect back to back contributions because normally they're not allowed Hmm, did you finish the previous contribution correctly before the "unknown session id"? no I wonder if for the test ceremony, there's a 5 minute timeout on contributions there's code which prevents you from logging in if the sequencer is currently waiting for a contribution from you, which makes sense so if the sequencer was still awaiting your contribution from the last ceremony, and the timeout was 5 minutes, then it'd give you "unknown session id" if you tried again with a new client Makes sense, but maybe a different error code would be better here Probably <CarlBeek> > <CarlBeek> unfortunately i don’t have access, i believe only @kevaundray does (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <PlasmaPower> I have no idea who runs it but do you know who'd be able to check the sequencer logs?) <CarlBeek> > <CarlBeek> this sounds very plausible (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <PlasmaPower> so if the sequencer was still awaiting your contribution from the last ceremony, and the timeout was 5 minutes, then it'd give you "unknown session id" if you tried again with a new client) I'm going to make a PR to give it a new error message 🙂 It would be great for a client to be able to get the batchcontribution again if they f' up <CarlBeek> that’d be useful, thanks In fact, we could probably just yeah send the batchcontribution back as <@360491619402776577> mentioned This 5 min delay makes debugging pretty horrible Feels like coding in rust 🧌 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> I don't have access to the logs anymore, @Recmo switched to a different fly.io server a while back (re @CarlBeek: unfortunately i don’t have access, i believe only @kevaundray does) <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Yeah, a development server that follows the production server that is essentially spammable would be good. Though I can see the rationale for lowering the timeout, moreso since there is no development server that has a lower timeout. Maybe you can open up an issue? I can't look into it right now, but would be good to track this (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <PlasmaPower> We should still consider lowering the timeout for contributions in the test server imo) Sure thing 🙂 ``` Response: {"code":"CeremonyError::PubKeyPairingFailed","error":"contribution invalid: Error in contribution 0: Pubkey pairing check failed"} ``` Yay one step further For updating the potPubKey I just need to scalar mult the previous potPubKey with the secret, right? Or only do g2^secret without using the previous potPubKey? hmm yeah I think the potPubKey should just be your pubkey, but I don't think this really matters, as the sequencer seems to always give you an initial potPubKey of one ```rs /// Creates the start of a new contribution. #[must_use] pub fn contribution(&self) -> Contribution { Contribution { powers: self.powers.clone(), pot_pubkey: G2::one(), bls_signature: BlsSignature::empty(), } } ``` I think the check that's failing is that `e(new_powers.g1[1], g2) != e(old_powers.g1[1], pot_pubkey)` in other words you should generate the new powers by multiplying the old ones by your secret I thought I did that, I might have an issue with copying the scalar Ah I think the issue is that scalar starts at your secret whereas perhaps it should start at one ``` scalar := &(*sec) scalars := make([]*blst.Scalar, transcript.NumG1Powers) for i := 0; i < transcript.NumG1Powers; i++ { scalars[i] = &(*scalar) var ok bool scalar, ok = scalar.Mul(sec) if !ok { panic("Scalar mult returned false") } } ``` my reading of the sequencer code is that it really starts at index one, in other words `x^1` The &(*) doesn't copy, so we overwrite the same scalar ah that might do it too I'll check in five minutes ;) hah gl If someone's around to review it I did make a PR to fix it https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-sequencer/pull/151 yep sure enough btw my go staticcheck is catching this: > &*x will be simplified to x. It will not copy x. (SA4001)go-staticcheck ah right I forgot go did this so silly nope still Here's what I'm trying: ``` one := make([]byte, 32) one[31] = 1 scalar := new(blst.Scalar).Deserialize(one) if scalar == nil { return errors.New("failed to generate one scalar") } scalars := make([]*blst.Scalar, transcript.NumG1Powers) for i := 0; i < transcript.NumG1Powers; i++ { copy := *scalar scalars[i] = &copy var ok bool scalar, ok = scalar.Mul(sec) if !ok { panic("Scalar mult returned false") } } ``` I think it worked! ``` Contribution calculated in 2.996714097s Submitting our contribution ``` and it exited Oh wow Very nice! thanks! feel free to steal that code of course, it'll be easier than creating a PR 🙂 <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Could I just keep asking the sequencer to serve me the contribution file while its my turn? (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <PlasmaPower> If someone's around to review it I did make a PR to fix it https://github.com/ethereum/kzg-ceremony-sequencer/pull/151) Oh but that code just sets your secret to 0 and wouldn't add any randomness^^ I don't think so. scalars[0] should be 1 and scalars[1] should be your secret <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> A secret of 0 should be rejected by the sequencer (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <MariusVanDerWijden> Oh but that code just sets your secret to 0 and wouldn't add any randomness^^) Is it that expensive compared to other endpoints? I could add a separate timeout of one per 5 seconds or something I guess it is a bit large <kevaundray> > <kevaundray> Just a suggestion since try_contribute is quite "simple" at the moment and is the one that should get hammered the most (re @kzg_ceremony_bot: <PlasmaPower> [reply]: Is it that expensive compared to other endpoints?) Well it'll only give back the current contribution to whoever's turn it is but I'll add a timeout *rate limiting Okay cool our implementation also seems to work, thanks <@165550481156866048>! nice! <Marcin> Btw. <@165550481156866048> can you please close and reopen that PR against newest master? Trying to get CI to run on it and I had to change some configs I'm just going to just push up a new commit to add rate limiting <Marcin> OK, let's see if that does it It might take me a bit longer than expected, so I tried closing and reopening.
